messages:
Jane S (support): Hey team — Escalation from AcmeCorp. After IdP cert rotation their users started getting 403s when POSTing SAMLResponse to our ACS. Customer says it worked for ~10m then started failing. Attach: customer trace and SAMLResponse snippet.

Acme logs: 
  saml.error: RecipientMismatch 'https://redwood.example.com/saml/acs' vs 'https://redwood.example.com/saml/acs/'

They also included a curl against https://idp.example.com/metadata that sometimes returns the new cert and sometimes the old one.

Mike O (eng-oncall): thanks jane — can you paste the raw response headers from the customer's curl? sounds like cache/proxy. also pinging @Tomas L for CDN/cache.

Jane S (support): headers attached, short: 
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=300
  Server: FastEdgeCDN/2.1
  Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2026 14:04:12 GMT

Priya K (security): Recipient mismatch + intermittent metadata = partial propagation of rotated key. Two possible causes: (1) IdP is returning mixed metadata (old and new) from different nodes, or (2) a caching layer is serving stale XML at some edges. If the SAMLResponse has the new signing cert but our ACS verification picks old key ordering or the ACS URL normalization fails (trailing slash), that yields RecipientMismatch.

Tomas L (infra): I ran repeated curls from a few regions — see below. Region A: metadata contains KeyDescriptor with SHA256=AAA (old). Region B: SHA256=BBB (new). So yes, CDN edge footprint is returning inconsistent files. Looks like the IdP published new metadata but the origin set Cache-Control=300 which caused edge inconsistencies during rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy finished for idp-metadata-rotation at 2026-03-15T13:57:00Z :white_check_mark:

Mike O (eng-oncall): repro steps (what I did): 
  1) curl -i https://idp.example.com/metadata 
  2) POST captured SAMLResponse to our test-acs endpoint 
  3) saw 403 + logs: "recipient mismatch" when the metadata at edge used old cert but SAMLResponse had new KeyInfo signing.

Sample SAML fragment (base64 decoded):
  <saml:SubjectConfirmationData Recipient=\"https://redwood.example.com/saml/acs\"/>
  Signature uses cert fingerprint BBB (new)

Jane S (support): Customer is asking for a quick mitigation — they have many users in the middle of rotation. What can we do on our side?

Priya K (security): Short term options: 
  - Accept both keys: add the old cert fingerprint (AAA) to our verified key set temporarily so both old and new signatures validate. That requires a config change and audit ticket.
  - Normalize ACS handling: tolerate trailing slash differences to reduce RecipientMismatch failures (we currently do strict compare).

Mike O (eng-oncall): I can enable dual-key acceptance for their tenant, but need an approved audit note. Which is fine for emergency. Also recommend a lightweight normalization layer to trim trailing slash and querystring before compare — low-risk fix.

Tomas L (infra): On the IdP side, best fix is to request their SRE to purge CDN edges or set Cache-Control: no-cache during rotation. For us, we can request Acme to re-push metadata via the federation portal or add versioned metadata URL (e.g., /metadata?v=2) to avoid edge cache collisions.

Alice C (customer-success): I told Acme we can do dual-key acceptance while they fix their metadata. They asked how long that will take. Mike, can you estimate time to enable for tenant 'acme-123'?

Mike O (eng-oncall): If security signs off, I can toggle dual-key in the tenant config and roll within 30–45m. Need Priya to confirm and Tomas to confirm no additional infra changes.

Priya K (security): I approve emergency dual-key for acme-123 for up to 24h, must log change and notify compliance. Please include justification: partial metadata propagation causing legitimate signed assertions to fail.

Tomas L (infra): I requested CDN invalidation from Acme's IdP SRE and also pushed an internal cache purge for our SAML metadata fetch process. They confirmed they cleared origin cache. Re-testing now.

Jane S (support): Re-test results from customer: after our change AND their CDN purge, log shows successful POSTs. They still saw a handful of failures for ~5m until all edges converged. Customer very thankful. :relieved:

Mike O (eng-oncall): Followups/actions: 
  - Create a small tenant config toggle for dual-key acceptance in case of future rotations (ticket INF-845).
  - Add trailing-slash normalizer for ACS compare (low-risk RFC, PR queued).
  - Recommend docs update for customers: 'perform metadata rotation with no-cache or versioned URL' (assign to docs).
  - Notify compliance about temporary key acceptance for acme-123 (audit log attached).

Priya K (security): Also remind customers to publish metadata with explicit validity window and rotate with a short TTL or use versioned endpoints. I'll draft a short KB.

Alice C (customer-success): I'll follow up with Acme and make sure they get the KB. Closing once docs + infra ticket are created.

Jane S (support): marking resolved for now; will re-open if customer reports more failures. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
